html:
The United States invaded Panama on 20 December 1989, in an operation called Just Cause, to remove the dictator Manuel Noriega. About 27,000 American troops took part.

President George H. W. Bush gave as reasons the protection of Americans, the canal treaties, democracy and the drug charges against Noriega. American forces quickly defeated the Panamanian army. Fires destroyed much of the poor neighbourhood of El Chorrillo near army headquarters. Hundreds of Panamanians died, many of them civilians; the exact number is disputed.

Noriega took refuge in the Vatican embassy, where American troops played loud rock music outside, and surrendered on 3 January 1990. Guillermo Endara, winner of the annulled election, became president. Panama abolished its army in 1994, as Costa Rica had done, and took over the canal in 1999 under the treaties.
sum: The United States invaded Panama on 20 December 1989, in an operation called Just Cause, to remove the dictator Manuel Noriega. About 27,000 American troops took part.
